kind: per-phase measurement, then the first end-to-end job through the studio API
why: The 2026-09-21 measured-once qualification began while a previous pass still held about 41 GiB, so its 30.4 GiB MemAvailable floor and its 74-90 GiB active envelope describe a contaminated host. This run measured the pack from a clean host and then proved the whole client path against it.

stack.weights_verified: 7 files re-hashed against config/qwen-image-21-weights.json before the engine is advertised (verify_pack, 14.0 s with warm page cache)

method.host_state: nvidia-smi reported no compute process and MemAvailable was 117.10 GiB before the run
method.sampling: 0.25 s, both psutil.virtual_memory().available and the per-process nvidia-smi allocation of the renderer
method.page_cache: image_render drops the checkpoint page cache before loading (posix_fadvise DONTNEED)
method.path: the job was submitted to the real studio API with a paired render ticket, not to the renderer directly

end_to_end.route: POST /api/gate -> GET /api/studio/engines -> POST /api/studio/jobs -> GET /api/studio/jobs/{id} -> GET /api/studio/jobs/{id}/content -> POST /api/studio/jobs/{id}/library
end_to_end.release: device allocation returned to 0 MiB and MemAvailable to 117.01 GiB once the resident was reaped

supersedes.envelope: cold_load 62-78 / warm_idle 34-46 / active_inference 74-90 GiB, which this run does not support

kept_fail_closed: warm_idle carries the pack's worst observed consumption (48.0 GiB) rather than the 40.7 GiB warm-steady figure, because the pair with the protected language primary would then land within about 1 GiB of the pool; co-residency stays refused until a visible-queue canary satisfies the companion qualification rule.
open_items: co-residency with the protected primary is still unqualified (needs the visible-queue canary)
config/gpu-capacity-receipts.json still carries the retired ComfyUI 'image' budget (peak_gib 15.0); which engine that entry should now describe is a call for Steve
the image host pins the interpreter file's sha256, not the installed package set, so the hash-locked requirements file is the only thing keeping the environment reproducible
